chunks: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn 'Uqda al-Hafiz al-Hamdani, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn al-Mufaddal ibn Ibrahim al-Ash'ari, who said: Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Ziyad (who is al-Wassah al-Kazzaz, and is the son of Bint Ilyas) narrated to us; he paused then returned and cut off the chain, from Abd al-Karim ibn 'Umar al-Kath'ami, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Ya'fur, and Mu'alla ibn Khunays, from Abu al-Samit, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The greatest of the major sins are seven: Shirk with Allah the Great, and killing the soul which Allah has forbidden except with the right, and eating the wealth of orphans, and disobedience to parents, and charging chaste women with unchastity, and fleeing from the battle line, and denying what Allah the Mighty and Majestic has revealed.

As for Shirk with Allah the Great, there has reached you what Allah revealed concerning us and what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, so return it to Allah and to His Messenger.
And as for killing the sacred soul, it is the killing of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and his companions.
And as for eating the wealth of orphans, we were wronged regarding our Fai' (booty/wealth) and they took it.

And as for disobedience to parents, indeed Allah the Mighty and Majestic said in His Book: 'The Prophet is more worthy of the believers than themselves, and his wives are their mothers.' And he is a father to them, so they were disobedient to him in his offspring and in his close relatives.
And as for charging chaste women with unchastity, they charged Fatimah (peace be upon her) with it on their pulpits.
And as for fleeing from the battle line, they gave the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) the pledge of allegiance willingly, not being coerced, then they fled from him and abandoned him.
And as for denying what Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed, they denied our right and rejected it, and this is something in which no one can be confused.
And Allah says: 'If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your evil deeds and admit you to a noble entrance [into Paradise].'

The third part of the book Tahdhib al-Ahkam ended, and its end is the book of Zakat with the additions, and it is followed by the fourth part of the book of As-Siyam. 'And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.'

key_terms.فَيْئَنَا: Our booty/wealth (specifically of the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What are the seven greatest major sins according to Imam al-Sadiq in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) enumerates the seven greatest major sins (al-Kaba'ir), linking each to specific historical events or Quranic concepts relevant to the Ahl al-Bayt. These include Shirk, the killing of Husayn (peace be upon him), eating orphans' wealth (referring to the deprivation of the Prophet's family's Fai'), disobedience to parents (referring to the Prophet's family), charging chaste women (referring to Fatimah), fleeing from battle (referring to the Sahaba after Ali), and denying divine right. This hadith is significant in Shia jurisprudence for establishing the theological weight of the Ahl al-Bayt's historical grievances as major sins.
